hypothesis: Adding hour-of-day and strictly-earlier user-gap categorical fields will improve within-user ordering by giving the DeepFM more legal context-dependent interaction signal for each (user,candidate-item) pair.
implementation_plan: Apply the trusted catalog operator legal_temporal_context exactly as registered, which edits only the features block by adding categorical hour and strictly-earlier user exposure-gap buckets through SO.build_features consumer-visible config. No other blocks change.
justification: This is the required first-round exploit for the current baseline parent and is directly connected to an executable consumer in the delegated backend. Because metrics rank within user, context features that vary by impression can change ordering, unlike per-user constants.
observation: The trusted operator catalog marks "legal_temporal_context" with search_priority="first_round_exploit" and says it "Adds hour and strictly-earlier exposure-gap buckets without evaluation feedback." The runtime contract states supported feature keys are "hour" and "user_gap" inside SO.build_features.
research_nonuse_reason: A directly applicable trusted operator exists and is the more precise basis than external research here; the key requirement is using a connected first-round exploit already supported by SO.build_features.
risk: Added fields may overlap with signal already learned by the FM and yield only tiny gain
